message.content:
Since \(\frac{1+\sqrt5}{4}=\cos 36^\circ\), we have
\[
2\theta=\pm 36^\circ+360^\circ k \quad\Rightarrow\quad \theta=\pm 18^\circ+180^\circ k.
\]
Because \(\tan^2\) is even and periodic, we can take \(\theta=18^\circ\). Then
\[
\tan^2\theta\tan^2 3\theta=\tan^2 18^\circ\tan^2 54^\circ.
\]

Let \(t=\tan 18^\circ\). Since \(\cos 36^\circ=\cos(2\cdot18^\circ)\),
\[
\frac{1-t^2}{1+t^2}=\frac{1+\sqrt5}{4}.
\]
Solving gives
\[
t^2=\tan^2 18^\circ=\frac{5-2\sqrt5}{5}.
\]

Also, \(54^\circ=90^\circ-36^\circ\), so
\[
\tan 54^\circ=\cot 36^\circ.
\]
Now
\[
\cos^2 36^\circ=\left(\frac{1+\sqrt5}{4}\right)^2=\frac{3+\sqrt5}{8},
\]
so
\[
\sin^2 36^\circ=1-\frac{3+\sqrt5}{8}=\frac{5-\sqrt5}{8}.
\]
Thus
\[
\tan^2 54^\circ=\cot^2 36^\circ
=\frac{\cos^2 36^\circ}{\sin^2 36^\circ}
=\frac{3+\sqrt5}{5-\sqrt5}
=\frac{5+2\sqrt5}{5}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\tan^2 18^\circ\tan^2 54^\circ
=\frac{5-2\sqrt5}{5}\cdot\frac{5+2\sqrt5}{5}
=\frac{25-20}{25}
=\frac15.
\]

The answer is \(\boxed{\frac15}\).
